facts.text: Leverage has been flat, not falling. EBITDA growth is the only thing holding the ratio: last-twelve-months EBITDA is USD 1,246.945 million against USD 1,214.111 million for 2025, while net debt rose USD 104.059 million since the 2025 year end, so a flat or falling EBITDA would raise leverage immediately. Basis: calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18

facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: Shareholder payments, not debt reduction, are the main use of free cash flow. Dividends and share repurchases took USD 464.363 million in the nine months, about 78.1% of free cash flow, and the same period spent a further USD 73.262 million on acquisitions, USD 72.419 million on the new headquarters, USD 16.506 million on real estate and USD 40.737 million on tax credit equity investments. Together these exceeded free cash flow, so debt and cash absorbed the gap; the remaining repurchase authorization was USD 498.8 million at the quarter end and a further USD 18.2 million was spent after it. A creditor should expect leverage to stay near four times while this policy continues. Basis: calculation C06; calculation C08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20

Capacity as the issuer states it serves liquidity, carrying value serves leverage, and principal serves maturity work.
Basis: calculation C05; calculation C09; Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25

facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the combination of rising EBITDA, interest cover near five times, a reported covenant ratio well inside its maximum and more than USD 1.5 billion of undrawn capacity. What would change the view is a decline in funeral volumes, which the issuer cites in lowering its fourth-quarter outlook, repurchases continuing at the current pace, or a rise in floating rates, since the revolver and term loan bear floating rates. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_exhibit991q326earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C05

rows.label: Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- High: The issuer states no EBITDA and the credit agreement that defines its covenant ratio is not supplied, so the leverage level depends on a derived definition. Derived net debt to EBITDA is above the issuer's ratio in every period shown, and adding back amortization of cemetery property closes most of the difference; the level cannot be tied to the covenant. The agreement's definition would close this. Basis: calculation C05; calculation C09; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25 - Medium: Executed financing documents are not supplied, so security, legal ranking, guarantors, reference rates, spreads, floors, scheduled amortisation and the terms of the headquarters construction facility are not established, and instrument carrying values are not separately disclosed. This restricts the debt stack, the EBITDA bridge and any secured-leverage or priority conclusion to not supplied rather than zero. The executed credit agreement dated 2025-11-20 and the senior indenture with its supplements would close it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; Source readiness (CP-0) - Medium: The letter-of-credit disclosures conflict: each report says the letters of credit were replaced by a surety bond in the second quarter of 2025, yet the same reports show letters of credit outstanding afterwards and closed in 2026. Undrawn capacity is used as the issuer states it at each date, which restricts nothing in the ratios but leaves the true capacity at each date unconfirmed. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; Source readiness (CP-0) - Medium: The amount of cash that is encumbered by Canadian balances and minimum operating needs is not stated, and borrowing capacity at 2024-12-31 is not stated. Net debt subtracts cash as printed, so net leverage is understated to the extent cash is not freely available, and the 2024 liquidity point is not supplied. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102 - Low: The maturity ladder is printed only at 2025-12-31 and its caption conflicts with its total, which equals total debt after issuance costs. Reconciling items are therefore zero on the printed ladder, and refinancing timing at later dates rests on current maturities. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; calculation C14; Source readiness (CP-0) - Low: The floating-rate disclosures conflict: the debt note gives a weighted average floating rate at 2026-09-30 that differs from the nine-month figure in the management discussion, and the first- and second-quarter discussions give a smaller decline than the third. Coverage uses cash interest paid, so no ratio depends on either rate, but forward interest cost cannot be set from these sources. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; 10-Q_2026-03-31_sci-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-06-30_sci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 40; Source readiness (CP-0) - Low: No source reports the fourth quarter of 2025 alone, and interim cash taxes paid are not printed in the quarterly reports. Last-twelve-months figures are built from the year plus stub less prior stub, which needs no quarter, but a discrete fourth-quarter series and an interim cash-tax series are not supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–8; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 97; calculation C04 - Low: Maintenance against growth capital expenditure is printed for interim periods in the earnings releases but only as year-on-year changes in the annual report, and it was not extracted here, so only total capital expenditures are carried. Unlevered free cash flow is not calculable because gross cash interest and the tax shield are not established. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27 - Low: Interim cash interest is printed in USD millions to one decimal, restricted cash at interim dates is derived from the cash flow closing balance, and the first-quarter balance sheet shows an income tax receivable line that the other balance sheets include in Other. These limit precision, not direction, and no missing balance is treated as zero. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-03-31_sci-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 7 - Low: Source dashes (the restructuring charge in 2023 and in some quarters) and lines that the interim statements do not print (restructuring in the first quarter, losses on early extinguishment of debt, debt issuance costs and other investing activities, and the annual-only income taxes paid) are carried as missing, not zero. Every statement identity still ties, so no total depends on a missing line; operating lease liabilities and the retirement benefit obligation are printed only at year ends. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 71; 10-Q_2026-03-31_sci-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 105; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 113 - Low: The issuer's adjusted measures, earnings excluding special items and adjusted operating cash flow, are not EBITDA and are not used in any ratio, and the earnings releases for the first and second quarters were inventoried but no figure was taken from them. Nothing in the leverage or cover figures depends on them. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_exhibit991q326earningsrele.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18

facts.text: - The business is a scaled, backlog-supported consolidator, not a transaction story. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Cemetery earnings lean on trust income and on the timing of property recognition. Trust fund income was USD 313.3 million in 2025, the trusts hold about 60% in equities, and they returned 15.1% in 2025 and 6.2% in the first nine months of 2026, so a market fall would cut recognized revenue and could force replenishment in states that require it; unrealized losses in those states were USD 0.6 million at the end of 2025 and no top-up is expected. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against caution is the covenant ratio of 3.69x against a 5.00x maximum, a preneed backlog that grew 4.17% in nine months, steady pricing, and 2025 operating cash flow of USD 942.8 million against payouts equal to 68.37% of it; buybacks are also discretionary and management can slow them at any time. A proxy statement showing no controlling holder and independent oversight of capital returns, restricted-payment baskets that bind well before the leverage target, and funeral volumes stabilising so that margin recovers would each strengthen the credit view. Further falls in comparable funeral services after the October outlook cut, trust returns turning negative enough to require replenishment, loss of surety capacity, or payouts continuing above free cash flow while leverage moves above the 4.0x target would weaken it. facts.label: Overall governance view
facts.text: Overall, SERVICE CORPORATION INTERNATIONAL presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is distributions that exceeded free cash flow in 2025 and stayed heavy in 2026, which matters because buybacks raise net debt unless earnings grow, so creditor protection rests on management discretion and an issuer-stated leverage target of 3.5x to 4.0x. Countervailing evidence is a covenant ratio of 3.69x against 5.00x, extended maturities and clear reporting. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed credit agreement and indenture, and the terms of the May 2026 charter amendment and bylaws filing. Governance review completed with limitations. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 122; calculation C09

facts.text: - The business profile is strong because revenue is contracted before it is earned, not because of size alone. Preneed contracts supplied 48.43% of 2025 revenue and the backlog of USD 17.72 billion is 3.43x total debt, up 4.17% since the end of 2025. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against caution is the issuer's reported covenant ratio of 3.69x against a 5.00x maximum, interest cover of 4.87x, free cash flow that exceeded payouts in the first nine months of 2026, and and, on a before-tax illustration, a repeat of this year's funeral decline that would lift derived net leverage only to 4.12x, below the 2026-06-30 peak of 4.14x. Because the covenant definition is not supplied, the gap between 3.69x and the derived 4.01x cannot be reconciled; Financial foundation notes that adding back amortization of cemetery property would bring the derived figure close to the issuer's, which suggests but does not establish the definition. Funeral volumes stabilising, payouts falling back below free cash flow, and a covenant definition showing wide headroom would strengthen the view. A second year of falling volumes, trust returns turning negative enough to force replenishment, loss of surety capacity, or leverage moving above 4.0x while buybacks continue would weaken it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C07; calculation C10

facts.label: Company description
facts.text: The issuer sells funeral and cemetery goods, services and property across North America, at need and on a preneed basis, and describes itself as the largest provider in the region. Funeral operations were 55.82% of 2025 revenue and cemeteries 44.18%, with 95.03% earned in the United States, and the footprint grew by six funeral locations and six cemeteries between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30. The credit linkage is revenue visibility: preneed sales are contracted years before delivery, price-guaranteed and funded through trusts or insurance, so cash flow depends less on the number of deaths in any one year than an at-need business would, while the funeral side stays tied to volume and a largely fixed cost base. Preneed funds are held in trusts or insurance policies and cannot be used freely for debt service. facts.label: Ownership and group structure

facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is largely recurring and regulated and less cyclical than discretionary consumer spending, with demand that the issuer describes as deferred rather than lost, and it is predictable at the contract level but variable with deaths and flu seasons. Volume is the weak driver: comparable funeral services fell 0.83% in 2025 and 2.66% in the first nine months of 2026, while the first quarter alone fell 6% on a strong prior-year flu season. Price and mix partly offset it, with revenue per service up 2.92% in 2025 and 3.17% in the nine months, even as cremation, which earns less per case, reached 64.9% of comparable cases. Preneed contracts are price-guaranteed, so inflation in goods and labour is the issuer's risk until trust earnings and pricing catch up. No customer concentration is disclosed, switching costs are local reputation and convenience, and the evidence supports a revenue base that is predictable in total and exposed in funeral volume. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: The issuer calls both businesses high fixed-cost, and the observed response confirms it: a 2.66% fall in comparable funeral services came with a 6.95% fall in comparable funeral gross profit, and the comparable funeral margin dropped to 19.2% from 20.8%. Salaries and fringe benefits are 27.89% of funeral revenue and facilities 11.32%, while cemetery selling compensation is 18.11% of cemetery revenue and rose with preneed production and higher guaranteed hourly wages. Healthcare costs also rose. Cost cuts have limits because licensed staff and facilities do not scale with volume, and the margin defence is price and cemetery mix. Corporate expenses fell in 2026 on lower share-return-linked incentive pay, a favorable legal settlement and favorable self-insurance reserve adjustments, which are not a recurring source of margin. Margins can be defended under mild volume pressure but not under a second year of declines without cost action. facts.label: Porter's five forces
facts.text: Rivalry is moderate because most competitors are small local operators and the issuer estimates about 18% share, so price competition comes from independents, low-cost providers and casket retailers rather than from a few large peers, which caps pricing in the funeral business. New entrants face low to moderate barriers in funeral service but high barriers in cemeteries because of land, permitting and capital, which protects cemetery earnings. Cremation is the main substitute, at 64.4% of comparable cases in 2025, and it earns less per case, which drags average revenue unless memorialization is sold. Buyers are individual families with itemized price disclosure under the Funeral Rule, which limits price discretion at need but is offset by preneed contracts that fix price. Suppliers of caskets and merchandise and the licensed funeral workforce matter more than any single vendor, and tariffs and wages are the credit-relevant risks. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33

facts.label: Political, economic, social and technology factors
facts.text: Regulatory and economic factors are material to credit and the social and technology factors are secondary. The Funeral Rule has been under federal review since 2020, state laws govern preneed trusts and surety use, about forty states are auditing unused preneed trust funds, and the annual report lists proposals that could prohibit common ownership of funeral homes and cemeteries in the same market, which matters because the issuer has the largest number of combination locations. Economic factors act through inflation and trust returns, which fed 2025 trust income and could reverse. Social factors are an ageing population, which the issuer expects to lift atneed results as preneed contracts mature, and a rising cremation share. Technology is mainly digital lead generation and an AI governance committee, neither of which moves credit quality. facts.label: Credit-translated SWOT
facts.text: Strengths: the preneed backlog and recurring revenue, scale and market share, a cemetery segment with high barriers, extended maturities and a reported covenant ratio well inside its maximum, and transparent controls. Weaknesses: derived leverage at the top of the target range, a fixed funeral cost base, payouts above free cash flow, market-sensitive trust income, and missing proxy and credit-agreement detail. Opportunities that could improve credit quality: preneed production growth converting to recognized revenue, a stabilising funeral volume, and monetization of the old headquarters buildings. Threats: a second year of falling volumes, a trust market fall that requires replenishment, loss of surety capacity, and rule changes on preneed funds or common ownership. facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: Scale and market position is strong because the issuer holds about 18% of North American funeral and cemetery revenue and operates the largest footprint, which absorbs local shocks. Competitive advantage is average, with the cemetery barriers, combination locations and the preneed backlog as its strongest elements and little pricing power in funeral service. Business diversification is average: two segments and about 5% of revenue from Canada, but every dollar is deathcare. Cost and capex flexibility is average, with a fixed funeral cost base and a small growth component in capital expenditure. Margin stability is average and weakening in funeral, where the comparable margin fell 1.6 percentage points in nine months. Free cash flow stability is average because conversion improved but with timing help and payouts above free cash flow in 2025. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is strong near term, with maturities extended to 2030 and liquidity covering current maturities 8.65 times, and untested beyond. Liquidity position is strong at USD 1,513.7 million of undrawn capacity, with encumbered cash not quantified. Financial policy and governance is average, with transparent reporting and a stated leverage target offset by payouts above free cash flow and a thin governance record. Main supports are the backlog, scale and liquidity; constraints are derived leverage at the top of the target range and funeral volume; the trend is stable with margin pressure; missing data are the covenant definition and the proxy statement. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the issuer's own outlook points to lower earnings growth than first expected: full-year adjusted earnings per share of USD 3.94 to USD 4.04 against a range of USD 4.10 to USD 4.30 set in July, with the midpoint of adjusted operating cash flow guidance, about USD 1,085 million, maintained and maintenance capital expenditure of USD 335 million. Pressure on margin and leverage is the near-term effect; the long-term effect is more recognized preneed revenue. facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is another year of falling funeral volume, as in the first nine months of 2026, while market returns weaken. The first operational break is funeral gross margin: at the observed ratio of 2.61x, a repeat of the 2.66% volume fall would cut funeral gross profit by about 6.95%, or USD 34.46 million on the 2025 base, before cost action and tax. Financial transmission is small on its own: derived EBITDA would fall to USD 1,212.485 million and net leverage would rise to 4.12x with cover of 4.73x. The larger threat is compounding: lower trust returns reduce recognized trust income, a loss of surety capacity could require about USD 258.7 million of trust funding, and payouts continuing at the 2026 pace would hold derived leverage near the top of the target range and push it above if earnings fell. Management levers are large relative to the shock: buybacks of USD 318.942 million in nine months, growth capital expenditure, acquisitions and headquarters spending can all be slowed, and USD 1,513.7 million of revolver capacity is undrawn. ## Findings
### Bottom line
Derived reported EBITDA covers cash interest 4.87x and net debt stands at 4.01x EBITDA for the last twelve months to 2026-09-30, so creditors face stable rather than falling leverage.

Net debt to EBITDA was 4.00x at the end of 2024 and 4.03x at the end of 2025. Net debt rose over the nine months because repurchases, dividends, acquisitions and headquarters construction together outran free cash flow, and EBITDA growth only held the ratio steady. The issuer states no EBITDA and prints a covenant ratio of 3.69x against a 5.00x maximum on a definition that is not supplied, so these figures cannot be rebuilt into it.

### Financial interpretation

Leverage has been flat, not falling. Total debt to derived EBITDA ran between 4.15x and 4.35x and net debt to EBITDA between 4.00x and 4.14x across the five balance-sheet dates, peaking at the end of June 2026 when the revolver balance rose to USD 365.000 million, and easing at the end of September as the revolver fell to USD 235.000 million and cash fell to USD 172.653 million. EBITDA growth is the only thing holding the ratio: last-twelve-months EBITDA is USD 1,246.945 million against USD 1,214.111 million for 2025, while net debt rose USD 104.059 million since the 2025 year end, so a flat or falling EBITDA would raise leverage immediately.
Basis: calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18

Cash interest is covered comfortably and the cover is improving. Derived EBITDA covers cash interest paid 4.87x on the last twelve months against 4.80x for 2025, because last-twelve-months EBITDA is up 2.70% on 2025 while cash interest is up 1.34%. After capital expenditures the cover is the 3.30x shown in the register, which is the more relevant measure for an issuer that spends about 9% of revenue on capital expenditures.
Basis: calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C06

Cash-flow quality improved but part of the gain is not structural. Free cash flow, operating cash flow less capital expenditures, was USD 594.241 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 467.042 million a year earlier, and its conversion of EBITDA is 54.65% on the last twelve months against 45.65% for 2025. The quarterly report lists a USD 49.0 million fall in cash tax payments among the drivers of the nine-month increase, and the earnings release ties a USD 29.9 million working-capital benefit in the third quarter to the timing of an extra payroll cycle in the prior-year period, so the run rate is lower than the latest figure suggests.
Basis: calculation C06; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_exhibit991q326earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

Shareholder payments, not debt reduction, are the main use of free cash flow. Dividends and share repurchases took USD 464.363 million in the nine months, about 78.1% of free cash flow, and the same period spent a further USD 73.262 million on acquisitions, USD 72.419 million on the new headquarters, USD 16.506 million on real estate and USD 40.737 million on tax credit equity investments. Together these exceeded free cash flow, so debt and cash absorbed the gap; the remaining repurchase authorization was USD 498.8 million at the quarter end and a further USD 18.2 million was spent after it. A creditor should expect leverage to stay near four times while this policy continues.
Basis: calculation C06; calculation C08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20

Liquidity is adequate against near-term maturities but thinner in cash than before. Cash of USD 172.653 million plus undrawn revolver capacity of USD 1,513.7 million gives USD 1,686.353 million, about 8.6 times the USD 195.060 million of current maturities, which include the notes due in April 2027. The year-end ladder puts USD 1,790.101 million in 2030 and USD 1,687.357 million after 2030, so the next large test is the 2030 refinancing, not the near term. The cash figure includes balances in Canada and minimum operating needs that the issuer calls encumbered without giving an amount, so unrestricted cash is lower than shown.
Basis: calculation C07; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101

Customer prepayments are a large non-debt funding source and not ordinary payables. Deferred revenue, net rose to USD 1,820.555 million from USD 1,779.266 million at the 2025 year end, deferred receipts held in trust to USD 6,050.706 million from USD 5,784.398 million and care trusts' corpus to USD 2,448.379 million from USD 2,381.507 million. They are backed by trust investments and preneed receivables on the asset side and, for part of the obligation, by surety bonds of USD 498.3 million posted in lieu of trusting funds, but the issuer must still deliver the merchandise and services, and trust investment values move with markets. A fall in trust values or in preneed sales would show first in operating cash flow and in the surety and funding commitments, not in the debt table.

Events after the quarter end are kept out of the period figures. The third-quarter report states repurchases after 2026-09-30 of USD 18.2 million without a date; applied to net debt at 2026-09-30 they give USD 5,018.495 million and 4.02x. No other post-period event that changes net debt is stated in the sources read.
Basis: calculation C08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20

Where the sources disagree, each figure is kept and its purpose stated. The issuer's covenant ratio is 3.69x at 2026-09-30 against a 5.00x maximum, while derived net debt to EBITDA is 4.01x; adding back amortization of cemetery property would give 3.70x, close to the issuer's figure, but no source states the covenant definition, so the closeness is an observation and not a reconstruction. The letter-of-credit wording, the maturity-ladder basis and the floating-rate figures conflict inside the filings and are carried as conflicts. Capacity as the issuer states it serves liquidity, carrying value serves leverage, and principal serves maturity work.
Basis: calculation C05; calculation C09; Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the combination of rising EBITDA, interest cover near five times, a reported covenant ratio well inside its maximum and more than USD 1.5 billion of undrawn capacity. What would change the view is a decline in funeral volumes, which the issuer cites in lowering its fourth-quarter outlook, repurchases continuing at the current pace, or a rise in floating rates, since the revolver and term loan bear floating rates.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_exhibit991q326earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C05

## Gaps

- High: The issuer states no EBITDA and the credit agreement that defines its covenant ratio is not supplied, so the leverage level depends on a derived definition. Derived net debt to EBITDA is above the issuer's ratio in every period shown, and adding back amortization of cemetery property closes most of the difference; the level cannot be tied to the covenant. The agreement's definition would close this.
Basis: calculation C05; calculation C09; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25

- Medium: Executed financing documents are not supplied, so security, legal ranking, guarantors, reference rates, spreads, floors, scheduled amortisation and the terms of the headquarters construction facility are not established, and instrument carrying values are not separately disclosed. This restricts the debt stack, the EBITDA bridge and any secured-leverage or priority conclusion to not supplied rather than zero. The executed credit agreement dated 2025-11-20 and the senior indenture with its supplements would close it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Medium: The letter-of-credit disclosures conflict: each report says the letters of credit were replaced by a surety bond in the second quarter of 2025, yet the same reports show letters of credit outstanding afterwards and closed in 2026. Undrawn capacity is used as the issuer states it at each date, which restricts nothing in the ratios but leaves the true capacity at each date unconfirmed.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Medium: The amount of cash that is encumbered by Canadian balances and minimum operating needs is not stated, and borrowing capacity at 2024-12-31 is not stated. Net debt subtracts cash as printed, so net leverage is understated to the extent cash is not freely available, and the 2024 liquidity point is not supplied.

- Low: The maturity ladder is printed only at 2025-12-31 and its caption conflicts with its total, which equals total debt after issuance costs. Reconciling items are therefore zero on the printed ladder, and refinancing timing at later dates rests on current maturities.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; calculation C14; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Low: The floating-rate disclosures conflict: the debt note gives a weighted average floating rate at 2026-09-30 that differs from the nine-month figure in the management discussion, and the first- and second-quarter discussions give a smaller decline than the third. Coverage uses cash interest paid, so no ratio depends on either rate, but forward interest cost cannot be set from these sources.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; 10-Q_2026-03-31_sci-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-06-30_sci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 40; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Low: No source reports the fourth quarter of 2025 alone, and interim cash taxes paid are not printed in the quarterly reports. Last-twelve-months figures are built from the year plus stub less prior stub, which needs no quarter, but a discrete fourth-quarter series and an interim cash-tax series are not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–8; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 97; calculation C04

- Low: Maintenance against growth capital expenditure is printed for interim periods in the earnings releases but only as year-on-year changes in the annual report, and it was not extracted here, so only total capital expenditures are carried. Unlevered free cash flow is not calculable because gross cash interest and the tax shield are not established.

- Low: Interim cash interest is printed in USD millions to one decimal, restricted cash at interim dates is derived from the cash flow closing balance, and the first-quarter balance sheet shows an income tax receivable line that the other balance sheets include in Other. These limit precision, not direction, and no missing balance is treated as zero.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-03-31_sci-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 7

- Low: Source dashes (the restructuring charge in 2023 and in some quarters) and lines that the interim statements do not print (restructuring in the first quarter, losses on early extinguishment of debt, debt issuance costs and other investing activities, and the annual-only income taxes paid) are carried as missing, not zero. Every statement identity still ties, so no total depends on a missing line; operating lease liabilities and the retirement benefit obligation are printed only at year ends.

- Low: The issuer's adjusted measures, earnings excluding special items and adjusted operating cash flow, are not EBITDA and are not used in any ratio, and the earnings releases for the first and second quarters were inventoried but no figure was taken from them. Nothing in the leverage or cover figures depends on them.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_exhibit991q326earningsrele.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18

## Findings
### Bottom line

SERVICE CORPORATION INTERNATIONAL is a listed deathcare consolidator with no sponsor or controlling holder named in the supplied filings; its USD 17.72 billion preneed backlog supports creditors, but payouts above 2025 free cash flow and the unsupplied proxy statement cap the governance view.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 122; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C09

Funeral volume is the weak point: comparable services fell 2.66% in the first nine months of 2026 and management cut its outlook in October, while cemetery growth and pricing offset it at group level. Dividends and buybacks took 116.30% of free cash flow in 2025 and 78.14% in the first nine months of 2026. The issuer's covenant ratio is 3.69x against a 5.00x maximum and its stated leverage target is 3.5x to 4.0x, but whether covenant limits bind payouts cannot be tested because the baskets are not supplied.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 41–44; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_exhibit991q326earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation C06; calculation C09
### Key findings

- **The business is a scaled, backlog-supported consolidator, not a transaction story.** Funeral operations produced 55.82% of 2025 revenue and cemeteries 44.18%, with 95.03% earned in the United States. About 48.43% of 2025 revenue was recognized from preneed contracts, and the preneed backlog of USD 17.01 billion at the end of 2025 was 3.95x annual revenue; it reached USD 17.72 billion by September 2026, up 4.17%. That gives creditors revenue visibility most consumer-service issuers lack, but USD 9.15 billion of the backlog is insurance-funded, sits off the balance sheet and depends on third-party insurers.

Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 115–116; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32

- **Funeral volume is the pressure point and it hits margin before revenue.** Comparable funeral services fell 2.66% in the first nine months of 2026 while average revenue per service rose 3.17%, and the comparable funeral gross margin dropped to 19.2% from 20.8% because staff, facility and vehicle costs largely do not fall with volume. Management cut its full-year adjusted earnings outlook to USD 3.94 to USD 4.04 per share in October 2026, citing lower funeral volumes than expected and higher healthcare, selling and marketing costs. Cemetery revenue rose 5.5% in the same nine months, and cemetery gross profit growth more than offset the funeral decline at group level.

Basis: calculation C06; calculation C07; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–45; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 33; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_exhibit991q326earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 4

- **Cemetery earnings lean on trust income and on the timing of property recognition.** Trust fund income was USD 313.3 million in 2025, the trusts hold about 60% in equities, and they returned 15.1% in 2025 and 6.2% in the first nine months of 2026, so a market fall would cut recognized revenue and could force replenishment in states that require it; unrealized losses in those states were USD 0.6 million at the end of 2025 and no top-up is expected. Preneed property sales production grew 7.1% in the nine months against 4.4% for recognized property revenue, which builds backlog but presses near-term cemetery margin.

- **Capital allocation favours shareholders over deleveraging.** Dividends and buybacks took 116.30% of free cash flow in 2025, buybacks alone costing USD 464.2 million, and carrying debt rose 6.30% over the year. In the first nine months of 2026 payouts were 78.14% of free cash flow, and in June 2026 the board added about USD 472.0 million to the repurchase authorization. The policy is deliberate and, on the issuer's own ratio, inside its limits; but buybacks are discretionary, so creditor protection depends on management slowing them if earnings weaken, since the restricted-payment baskets are not supplied.

Basis: calculation C09; calculation C10; calculation C11; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-06-30_sci-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19

- **Ownership is public and no sponsor is named, but the supplied record says little about board independence and committees.** The registrant is listed on the New York Stock Exchange, had fewer than three thousand holders of record at the end of 2025, and its cover page treats only directors and executive officers as affiliates. Ownership, related-party, compensation and committee disclosures are incorporated from a proxy statement that is not supplied, so extraction through fees or related-party payments cannot be tested. The chief executive, in post since 2005, has also been chairman since 2016, which a named lead independent director partly offsets; a charter amendment and a new bylaws filing from May 2026 are listed but their terms are not supplied.

- **Transactions are refinancing and organic growth rather than leveraged events.** The main 2025 action was the November 2025 bank refinancing, which replaced facilities due January 2028 with a USD 750.0 million term loan and a USD 1.75 billion revolver due November 2030. Acquisitions cost USD 101.7 million in 2025 for 22 funeral locations and 2 cemeteries, against USD 182.9 million in 2024, and a separate construction facility was funding a new headquarters. No senior notes were issued in 2025 or in the first nine months of 2026; the last issue was USD 800.0 million of notes due 2032 in 2024.

- **Preneed regulation and surety support are contingent calls on liquidity, not current stress.** Surety bonds stood at USD 498.3 million at September 2026, most of them posted instead of funding preneed trusts; if every surety company cancelled, the 2025 annual report says about USD 258.7 million would have to be replaced or paid into state-mandated trust accounts. Roughly forty states are auditing unused preneed trust funds, with audits resolved and nothing further to report in nineteen of them, and management cannot estimate the possible loss in the rest.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is the covenant ratio of 3.69x against a 5.00x maximum, a preneed backlog that grew 4.17% in nine months, steady pricing, and 2025 operating cash flow of USD 942.8 million against payouts equal to 68.37% of it; buybacks are also discretionary and management can slow them at any time. A proxy statement showing no controlling holder and independent oversight of capital returns, restricted-payment baskets that bind well before the leverage target, and funeral volumes stabilising so that margin recovers would each strengthen the credit view. Further falls in comparable funeral services after the October outlook cut, trust returns turning negative enough to require replenishment, loss of surety capacity, or payouts continuing above free cash flow while leverage moves above the 4.0x target would weaken it.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The supplied documents state no pending acquisition, disposal, sponsor transaction or new bond issue, and the settings supply no deal terms. The transactions that shape the credit are a bank refinancing, a headquarters construction loan, bolt-on acquisitions and a heavy share repurchase programme.

In November 2025 the issuer replaced its USD 2.2 billion bank agreement due January 2028 with a USD 2.5 billion agreement due November 2030, made of a USD 1.75 billion revolver and a USD 750.0 million term loan; it is guaranteed by a majority of the domestic subsidiaries and carries a maximum leverage covenant and limits on dividends and buybacks. During the first nine months of 2026 the issuer drew USD 530.0 million on the revolver, repaid USD 550.0 million, and added USD 56.1 million to the headquarters facility due February 2037, which stood at USD 110.852 million at September 2026. The last bond issue was USD 800.0 million of unsecured 5.75% notes due October 2032 in 2024.

Acquisitions were USD 101.7 million in 2025, of which USD 0.4 million was cash acquired, for 22 funeral service locations and 2 cemeteries, and USD 182.9 million in 2024, including two metropolitan acquisitions for USD 120.6 million of cash in the third quarter of 2024 that brought USD 97.768 million of goodwill. Net of cash acquired the cash flow statement shows USD 101.291 million in 2025 and USD 181.210 million in 2024. In the first nine months of 2026 business acquisitions cost USD 73.262 million against USD 65.098 million a year earlier; the number of locations bought is not stated. ### Overall governance view

Overall, SERVICE CORPORATION INTERNATIONAL presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is distributions that exceeded free cash flow in 2025 and stayed heavy in 2026, which matters because buybacks raise net debt unless earnings grow, so creditor protection rests on management discretion and an issuer-stated leverage target of 3.5x to 4.0x. Countervailing evidence is a covenant ratio of 3.69x against 5.00x, extended maturities and clear reporting. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed credit agreement and indenture, and the terms of the May 2026 charter amendment and bylaws filing. Governance review completed with limitations.

- High: The proxy statement is not supplied, so beneficial ownership, committee membership, the independence of most directors, related-party dealings and compensation are not established. This restricts the ownership and governance conclusions to what the annual report states, and a large holder or related-party leakage cannot be ruled out. Source readiness listed board composition as unavailable, but the signature page names ten directors and a lead independent director, so only their independence, committees and holdings are missing. The 2026 proxy statement would close it.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 122; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 126; Source readiness (CP-0)

- High: The executed credit agreement and senior indenture are not supplied, so restricted-payment baskets, the leverage definition, guarantors of the notes and security are not established. Payout capacity and covenant headroom cannot be sized and the structural ranking of the notes is not set.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Medium: The terms of the charter amendment and bylaws exhibit incorporated from the Form 8-K filed on 2026-05-08 are not supplied, so any change to voting, takeover protection or indemnification is not visible.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53

- Medium: Acquisition prices, earnings multiples, integration results and the number of locations bought in 2026 are not stated, so the return on acquisitions and any pro forma leverage are not calculable.

- Medium: The preferred preneed insurance provider is not named and concentration is not disclosed, although USD 9.15 billion of backlog is insurance-funded; the unclaimed property exposure in about forty states is not estimable. Both limit the quality assessment of the backlog.

- Low: The letter-of-credit, maturity ladder and floating-rate disclosures conflict and are kept open; the headquarters facility size, ranking and completion date are not stated; seasonality and customer concentration are not measured. None changes a conclusion in this module.

spans.text: ## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for SERVICE CORP INTERNATIONAL (legal name SERVICE CORPORATION INTERNATIONAL) as of 2026-11-05, on the full credit assessment pathway. Scope is business quality, financial profile, outlook, downside path and monitoring, built on the supplied analyses of source readiness, the financial foundation and business and governance, with the issuer's reports used to check them. No rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or position size is given.

No external sources were used. The run settings leave ratings, quotes, peers and deal terms blank, and a blank value is treated as not supplied, never as zero.
## Findings
### Bottom line

SERVICE CORPORATION INTERNATIONAL has a defensible, backlog-supported business and adequate liquidity, but its derived leverage sits at the top of the issuer's own target range, held there by earnings growth and discretionary payouts, so credit quality is stable rather than improving.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation C09; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Derived net leverage was 4.01x at 2026-09-30, or 4.02x pro forma for USD 18.2 million of repurchases made after that date, while the issuer reports its own covenant ratio at 3.69x against a target of 3.5x to 4.0x and a 5.00x maximum. Derived EBITDA covers cash interest 4.87x, and undrawn revolver capacity is USD 1,513.7 million. The primary downside path is another fall in funeral volume while payouts continue and trust returns weaken.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–20; calculation C01; calculation C06
### Key findings

- **The business profile is strong because revenue is contracted before it is earned, not because of size alone.** Preneed contracts supplied 48.43% of 2025 revenue and the backlog of USD 17.72 billion is 3.43x total debt, up 4.17% since the end of 2025. This gives creditors revenue visibility most consumer-service issuers lack, but the backlog is revenue, not cash, and USD 9.15 billion of it is insurance-funded and depends on third-party insurers.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32

- **Leverage is stable, not falling, and sits at the top of the issuer's target range on the derived measure.** Derived net leverage was 4.01x at 2026-09-30 and 4.02x pro forma for the USD 18.2 million of repurchases made after that date, and total debt was 4.15x derived EBITDA, while the issuer reports a covenant ratio of 3.69x, inside its target of 3.5x to 4.0x, on a definition that is not supplied. Earnings growth of 2.70% on 2025 held the derived ratio while net debt rose, so any fall in EBITDA lifts it at once.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42

- **Funeral volume is the weakest dimension and it reaches margin before revenue.** Comparable funeral services fell 2.66% in the first nine months of 2026 and comparable funeral gross profit fell 6.95%, a ratio of 2.61x, because most costs do not fall with volume. Cemetery growth and pricing have so far offset it at group level, and management cut its full-year outlook in October.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C07; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 41–44; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_exhibit991q326earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 4

- **Free cash flow is real but the 2026 improvement is partly timing, and payouts take most of it.** Free cash flow conversion of derived EBITDA was 54.65% for the last twelve months against 45.65% for 2025, helped by lower cash taxes and working-capital timing. Dividends and buybacks took 116.30% of free cash flow in 2025 and 78.14% in the first nine months of 2026, and with acquisitions, headquarters construction and tax credit investments the nine-month uses exceeded free cash flow.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C04; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

- **Liquidity and maturities give refinancing capacity for now, with 2030 the real test.** Liquidity covers current maturities 8.65x and the 2027 maturities 2.29x, and 67.66% of the year-end ladder falls due in 2030 or later. The bank facility and term loan now mature in 2030, so the next large refinancing is about four years away, though the 2027 notes come first.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 101–102

- **Governance is neutral to mildly negative on policy, not on evidence of extraction.** No sponsor or controlling holder is named, a lead independent director is named, controls were found effective and the covenant ratio is reported, but payouts above free cash flow, the unsupplied proxy statement and the unsupplied credit agreement leave creditor protection resting on management discretion.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C04

- **Contingent claims and floating rates are second-order but real.** Loss of surety capacity would require about USD 258.7 million to be replaced or funded into trusts, equal to 15.34% of liquidity, and roughly one fifth of debt reprices with rates, about USD 10.86 million of extra annual cash interest for each 100 bp.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C06; calculation C09; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is the issuer's reported covenant ratio of 3.69x against a 5.00x maximum, interest cover of 4.87x, free cash flow that exceeded payouts in the first nine months of 2026, and and, on a before-tax illustration, a repeat of this year's funeral decline that would lift derived net leverage only to 4.12x, below the 2026-06-30 peak of 4.14x. Because the covenant definition is not supplied, the gap between 3.69x and the derived 4.01x cannot be reconciled; Financial foundation notes that adding back amortization of cemetery property would bring the derived figure close to the issuer's, which suggests but does not establish the definition. Funeral volumes stabilising, payouts falling back below free cash flow, and a covenant definition showing wide headroom would strengthen the view. A second year of falling volumes, trust returns turning negative enough to force replenishment, loss of surety capacity, or leverage moving above 4.0x while buybacks continue would weaken it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C07; calculation C10
### Limitations

- No peer, rating or market-price data is supplied, so the judgement that the business profile is strong rests on the issuer's own scale, history and backlog and not on a comparison with other deathcare or leveraged issuers.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The issuer gives only a fourth-quarter and a full-year earnings range and no multi-year forecast, so the outlook over twelve to twenty-four months is a reasoned extension of reported trends and the downside is an illustration, not a projection.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_exhibit991q326earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991q226earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 4

- Trust holdings by state, withdrawal rules and the share of trust income recognized in revenue are not supplied, so how far a market fall would cut cemetery earnings or require replenishment is directional and cannot be sized.

- The fixed-rate share is stated only as approximately 79% and no hedging is disclosed, so the finding that floating-rate exposure is second-order rests on an approximate sensitivity, and the revolver and term loan could carry a larger share of the floating debt than assumed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C06
### Analytical appendix — complete canonical registers
The sections and tables below carry the credit steps and registers behind the passages above.
### Strengths and weaknesses

**Strength 1: contracted, backlog-supported revenue.** The preneed backlog of USD 17.72 billion at 2026-09-30 is revenue already sold, and about 48% of 2025 revenue was recognized from preneed contracts, so a volume fall hits a smaller share of income than in an at-need business. That supports debt service through a cycle, though the backlog is revenue and not cash and part sits off the balance sheet.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31

**Strength 2: scale and a funeral and cemetery mix.** Cemeteries produced 44.18% of 2025 revenue and 56.51% of segment gross profit, with a cemetery gross margin of 33.84% against 20.61% for funeral, so the cemetery side carries the group when funeral volumes fall. This is a real offset, but it relies on preneed property production and trust income.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C10

**Strength 3: maturities extended and liquidity in place.** The bank facility and term loan were refinanced to November 2030 and USD 1,513.7 million of revolver capacity is undrawn, covering current maturities 8.65 times. Refinancing pressure is therefore not near term.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102

**Strength 4: interest cover and reported covenant ratio.** Derived EBITDA covers cash interest 4.87 times and the issuer reports a covenant ratio of 3.69x against a 5.00x maximum, so a moderate earnings fall does not threaten debt service.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C01

**Strength 5: transparent reporting and controls.** Controls were audited and found effective, and the covenant ratio, debt by instrument and reconciled adjusted measures are reported each quarter, which supports monitoring.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 120–121

**Weakness 1: derived leverage at the top of the target range, held there by earnings growth and payouts.** Derived net leverage is 4.01x, or 4.02x pro forma for repurchases after 2026-09-30, while the issuer reports 3.69x against a 3.5x to 4.0x target, while dividends and buybacks took 116.30% of free cash flow in 2025. Creditors depend on management slowing buybacks if earnings weaken.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C04; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42

**Weakness 2: funeral volume and fixed costs.** Comparable funeral services fell 2.66% in nine months and comparable funeral gross profit fell 6.95%, so each point of volume cost about 2.61 points of gross profit. Management cut its outlook on lower volumes and higher costs.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C07; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_exhibit991q326earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 4

**Weakness 3: market-sensitive trust income and contingent calls.** Cemetery and preneed earnings depend on trust returns, replenishment can be required in some states, and loss of surety capacity would require about USD 258.7 million of trust funding.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C09

**Weakness 4: governance evidence is thin and policy favours payouts.** Ownership, committee and related-party disclosures sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, and restricted-payment baskets are not known, so alignment with creditors cannot be tested.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 122

**Weakness 5: floating-rate and refinancing exposure.** About one fifth of debt reprices with rates, and a third of the year-end ladder falls due before 2030, including the 2027 notes; a rate rise or a closed market would arrive while derived leverage is already at the top of the issuer's target range.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05; calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18

### Company description

The issuer sells funeral and cemetery goods, services and property across North America, at need and on a preneed basis, and describes itself as the largest provider in the region. Funeral operations were 55.82% of 2025 revenue and cemeteries 44.18%, with 95.03% earned in the United States, and the footprint grew by six funeral locations and six cemeteries between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30. The credit linkage is revenue visibility: preneed sales are contracted years before delivery, price-guaranteed and funded through trusts or insurance, so cash flow depends less on the number of deaths in any one year than an at-need business would, while the funeral side stays tied to volume and a largely fixed cost base. Preneed funds are held in trusts or insurance policies and cannot be used freely for debt service.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C08
### Ownership and group structure

The issuer is a listed public company with no sponsor or controlling holder named in the supplied filings; ten directors, including a lead independent director, signed the annual report and the chief executive is also chairman. Operating subsidiaries are owned directly or indirectly, a majority of the domestic subsidiaries guarantee the bank credit agreement, the guarantors of the senior notes are not stated, and the preneed and perpetual care trusts are consolidated but hold assets for customers and cemetery upkeep. The financial policy is explicit: a payout target of 30% to 40% of adjusted earnings plus buybacks, a leverage target of 3.5x to 4.0x, and bank covenants limiting dividends and repurchases. Creditor alignment is moderate because distributions exceeded free cash flow in 2025 while the issuer's reported covenant ratio stays inside its own target range, and the governance risk level from the business and governance analysis is Medium.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is largely recurring and regulated and less cyclical than discretionary consumer spending, with demand that the issuer describes as deferred rather than lost, and it is predictable at the contract level but variable with deaths and flu seasons. Volume is the weak driver: comparable funeral services fell 0.83% in 2025 and 2.66% in the first nine months of 2026, while the first quarter alone fell 6% on a strong prior-year flu season. Price and mix partly offset it, with revenue per service up 2.92% in 2025 and 3.17% in the nine months, even as cremation, which earns less per case, reached 64.9% of comparable cases. Preneed contracts are price-guaranteed, so inflation in goods and labour is the issuer's risk until trust earnings and pricing catch up. No customer concentration is disclosed, switching costs are local reputation and convenience, and the evidence supports a revenue base that is predictable in total and exposed in funeral volume.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C07; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 41–43; EX-99.1_2026-04-29_exhibit991q126earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Cost structure and margin resilience

The issuer calls both businesses high fixed-cost, and the observed response confirms it: a 2.66% fall in comparable funeral services came with a 6.95% fall in comparable funeral gross profit, and the comparable funeral margin dropped to 19.2% from 20.8%. Salaries and fringe benefits are 27.89% of funeral revenue and facilities 11.32%, while cemetery selling compensation is 18.11% of cemetery revenue and rose with preneed production and higher guaranteed hourly wages. Healthcare costs also rose. Cost cuts have limits because licensed staff and facilities do not scale with volume, and the margin defence is price and cemetery mix. Corporate expenses fell in 2026 on lower share-return-linked incentive pay, a favorable legal settlement and favorable self-insurance reserve adjustments, which are not a recurring source of margin. Margins can be defended under mild volume pressure but not under a second year of declines without cost action.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C07; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 41–45; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_exhibit991q326earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Capital intensity and free cash flow conversion

Capital expenditure is about 9% of revenue, and 82.22% of nine-month 2026 spending was maintenance, cemetery development and other required spend against 17.78% growth, so the flexible part is small. Free cash flow conversion of derived EBITDA was 54.65% for the last twelve months against 45.65% for 2025, but the issuer attributes part of the gain to a USD 49.0 million fall in cash taxes and working-capital timing. Cash interest of USD 256.301 million is covered 4.87x by derived EBITDA and 3.30x after capital expenditures. EBITDA turns into durable free cash flow for debt service, but the 2026 conversion should not be extrapolated, and after payouts, acquisitions, headquarters construction and tax credit investments the nine-month uses exceeded free cash flow by USD 73.046 million.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C04; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_exhibit991q326earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 17
### Porter's five forces

Rivalry is moderate because most competitors are small local operators and the issuer estimates about 18% share, so price competition comes from independents, low-cost providers and casket retailers rather than from a few large peers, which caps pricing in the funeral business. New entrants face low to moderate barriers in funeral service but high barriers in cemeteries because of land, permitting and capital, which protects cemetery earnings. Cremation is the main substitute, at 64.4% of comparable cases in 2025, and it earns less per case, which drags average revenue unless memorialization is sold. Buyers are individual families with itemized price disclosure under the Funeral Rule, which limits price discretion at need but is offset by preneed contracts that fix price. Suppliers of caskets and merchandise and the licensed funeral workforce matter more than any single vendor, and tariffs and wages are the credit-relevant risks.
### Political, economic, social and technology factors

Regulatory and economic factors are material to credit and the social and technology factors are secondary. The Funeral Rule has been under federal review since 2020, state laws govern preneed trusts and surety use, about forty states are auditing unused preneed trust funds, and the annual report lists proposals that could prohibit common ownership of funeral homes and cemeteries in the same market, which matters because the issuer has the largest number of combination locations. Economic factors act through inflation and trust returns, which fed 2025 trust income and could reverse. Social factors are an ageing population, which the issuer expects to lift atneed results as preneed contracts mature, and a rising cremation share. Technology is mainly digital lead generation and an AI governance committee, neither of which moves credit quality.
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths: the preneed backlog and recurring revenue, scale and market share, a cemetery segment with high barriers, extended maturities and a reported covenant ratio well inside its maximum, and transparent controls. Weaknesses: derived leverage at the top of the target range, a fixed funeral cost base, payouts above free cash flow, market-sensitive trust income, and missing proxy and credit-agreement detail. Opportunities that could improve credit quality: preneed production growth converting to recognized revenue, a stabilising funeral volume, and monetization of the old headquarters buildings. Threats: a second year of falling volumes, a trust market fall that requires replenishment, loss of surety capacity, and rule changes on preneed funds or common ownership.

### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position is strong because the issuer holds about 18% of North American funeral and cemetery revenue and operates the largest footprint, which absorbs local shocks. Competitive advantage is average, with the cemetery barriers, combination locations and the preneed backlog as its strongest elements and little pricing power in funeral service. Business diversification is average: two segments and about 5% of revenue from Canada, but every dollar is deathcare. Cost and capex flexibility is average, with a fixed funeral cost base and a small growth component in capital expenditure. Margin stability is average and weakening in funeral, where the comparable margin fell 1.6 percentage points in nine months. Free cash flow stability is average because conversion improved but with timing help and payouts above free cash flow in 2025. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is strong near term, with maturities extended to 2030 and liquidity covering current maturities 8.65 times, and untested beyond. Liquidity position is strong at USD 1,513.7 million of undrawn capacity, with encumbered cash not quantified. Financial policy and governance is average, with transparent reporting and a stated leverage target offset by payouts above free cash flow and a thin governance record. Main supports are the backlog, scale and liquidity; constraints are derived leverage at the top of the target range and funeral volume; the trend is stable with margin pressure; missing data are the covenant definition and the proxy statement.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sci-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the issuer's own outlook points to lower earnings growth than first expected: full-year adjusted earnings per share of USD 3.94 to USD 4.04 against a range of USD 4.10 to USD 4.30 set in July, with the midpoint of adjusted operating cash flow guidance, about USD 1,085 million, maintained and maintenance capital expenditure of USD 335 million. Company tailwinds are preneed production growth, pricing and lower floating interest rates than a year earlier; headwinds are lower funeral volumes, healthcare, selling and marketing costs, and an elevated payout pace. Over three to five years the sector tailwind is an ageing population and growing preneed sales, and the headwinds are cremation mix, regulation and trust returns. Pressure on margin and leverage is the near-term effect; the long-term effect is more recognized preneed revenue.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_exhibit991q326earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991q226earningsrele.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_sci-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 32
### Qualitative downside scenario

The initiating condition is another year of falling funeral volume, as in the first nine months of 2026, while market returns weaken. The first operational break is funeral gross margin: at the observed ratio of 2.61x, a repeat of the 2.66% volume fall would cut funeral gross profit by about 6.95%, or USD 34.46 million on the 2025 base, before cost action and tax. Financial transmission is small on its own: derived EBITDA would fall to USD 1,212.485 million and net leverage would rise to 4.12x with cover of 4.73x. The larger threat is compounding: lower trust returns reduce recognized trust income, a loss of surety capacity could require about USD 258.7 million of trust funding, and payouts continuing at the 2026 pace would hold derived leverage near the top of the target range and push it above if earnings fell. Management levers are large relative to the shock: buybacks of USD 318.942 million in nine months, growth capital expenditure, acquisitions and headquarters spending can all be slowed, and USD 1,513.7 million of revolver capacity is undrawn. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress; the exposure is leverage drifting above the top of the issuer's target range and a tighter refinancing market in 2030, not default.

### Overall credit view

Overall, SERVICE CORPORATION INTERNATIONAL presents a defensible business profile supported by a preneed backlog, scale and a cemetery segment, but credit quality is constrained by derived leverage at the top of its target range, a fixed funeral cost base and payouts above free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears adequate, because conversion improved to 54.65% of derived EBITDA but with timing help. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on holding derived net leverage near 4.01x (4.02x pro forma for repurchases made after 2026-09-30), on the 2027 notes being met from liquidity, and on market access in 2030. The primary downside path is another year of falling funeral volume with weaker trust returns while payouts continue. Further analysis would require the covenant definition, the proxy statement and any rating or market data. Fundamental credit review completed. Top risk: leverage drifting above the top of the target range through continued payouts while funeral earnings weaken.

## Gaps

- High: The covenant definition, restricted-payment baskets and executed credit agreement are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable and the gap between the issuer's covenant ratio and derived leverage is not reconciled. The leverage and payout conclusions therefore use the derived ratio and the issuer's reported figure side by side.

- High: The proxy statement is not supplied, so beneficial ownership, committee membership, the independence of most directors and related-party dealings are not established; the governance conclusion rests on disclosed policy and controls.

- Low: The letter-of-credit, maturity-ladder basis and floating-rate disclosures conflict inside the filings and are carried as conflicts; the floating-rate sensitivity uses the issuer's approximate fixed share and the year-end ladder is the only one printed.
